description: Compute the electronic-energy reaction profile of sequential C-H scission of methane on the ferromagnetic Ni(111) FCC surface, using separately calculated *CHx and *H adsorption states to construct the intermediates and final *C + 4*H endpoint.
user_prompt: Compute the sequential C-H scission reaction profile of methane on the Ni(111) FCC surface (space group Fm-3m). Starting from gas-phase CH4 and a clean slab, four C-H bonds are broken sequentially on a single carbon center, constructing the *CH3 + *H, *CH2 + 2*H, *CH + 3*H, and *C + 4*H intermediate energies from separately calculated adsorption states. This is a thermal catalysis case; use gas-phase CH4 as the carbon reference and calculate CHx (x = 0-3) and H adsorption states separately using consistent slab models and calculation settings, adding the H contribution according to the number of dissociated H atoms. Build the full four-step ladder as intermediate context. Report the cumulative electronic reaction energy delta_E_total of CH4(g) + 5* -> *C + 4*H (in eV).

references: Wang, Cao, Li, Wang & Jiao, Surf. Sci. 600, 3226 (2006)
Bengaard, Norskov, Sehested, Clausen, Nielsen, Molenbroek & Rostrup-Nielsen, J. Catal. 209, 365 (2002)
method.modeling: Use a Ni(111) slab with at least 4 layers, vacuum >= 15 Angstrom, and a 2x2x1 or larger surface cell; calculate CHx and H adsorbates separately in the preferred hollow-site manifold using consistent slab models and calculation settings while preserving the single-carbon dehydrogenation sequence.
method.rationale: Wang et al. report the PBE Ni(111) cumulative methane-dehydrogenation ladder constructed from separately calculated CHx and H adsorption energies relative to CH4(g) and clean slabs as 0.00, +0.16, +0.32, +0.02, and +0.62 eV; the endpoint is the scored delta_E_total = +0.62 eV. The first C-H scission and other stepwise energies are diagnostic context only when the final benchmark metric is the total electronic reaction energy. Bengaard et al. provide a qualitative RPBE/PW91 cross-check for methane activation on Ni, while the tolerance covers PBE implementation, slab thickness, coverage, and adsorption-site differences.
